subject: Post-demo: extended context eval — model recommendations & mutual action plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@medtechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: extended context eval — model recommendations & mutual action plan

Hi Julia — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

Recap (from today's call)
- Goal: Evaluate a long-context pipeline for MedTechCo's clinical notes ingestion and downstream summarization for clinician workflows (expected avg doc ~45k tokens, occasional >120k).
- Primary success metrics: summarization fidelity (ROUGE/clinician-rated), no loss of critical entities (precision for meds/diagnoses), and 99th-percentile latency targets for extract+summarize flow (interactive target: <4s for extract, batch acceptable for full report).
- Constraints: PHI handling (we discussed SSO + VPC options), retention policy 90 days, dedicated audit logs.

What we need from you to scope an eval
1) Representative sample (redacted) of document set — preferred: 100 docs across the short/medium/long tails. If you can share a Drive link that’s ideal.
2) A short prioritized prompt set (2–3 golden prompts for extraction, 2 for summarization). I attached a stub CSV with example columns you can use.
3) Confirmation of SLOs (latency + fidelity thresholds) and whether interactive vs. async is acceptable for >60k tokens.

Our proposed model candidates & eval approach (high level)
- Candidate A: redwood-7b-long (optimized for longer context with fast decode; lower cost)
- Candidate B: redwood-70b-q4_long (higher quality for complex summarization; quantized for cost tradeoffs)
- Fallback: segment-and-stitch pattern (prefix caching + rolling KV + hierarchical summarization) to mitigate truncation risk.

Deliverables we propose for POC (2–3 week sprint)
- Setup: secure dataset ingest (S3+VPC), baseline runs on 100-sample set.
- Benchmarks: fidelity scores (ROUGE, entity-precision), token cost estimates, latency P50/P95/P99, truncation incidence report.
- Recommendations: quantization profile, batching/caching config, and a rollout plan for production.

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (recording), prompt-set-sample.csv (stub)

Proposed next steps
- You share sample dataset & confirm NDA/POC timing by EOD Tue (Aug 4).
- We'll run an initial baseline within 5 business days after dataset access.
- Quick sync Wed (Aug 5) if that works for your team for alignment.

Thanks — I’ll assign Neha and Dylan to lead the eval work on our side.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Looping in recommended technical plan and quick eval scope I drafted. High level:

- Model picks (based on tradeoffs)
  * redwood-7b-long: baseline for throughput/cost checks. Good for high-volume extract tasks with prefix caching.
  * redwood-70b-q4_long: quality-oriented baseline; quantization keeps cost reasonable while preserving summarization fidelity.

- Truncation approach options
  1) Full-window (if we can run on segmented disk-backed KV and the model variant supports >256k tokens) — fewer artifacts but higher cost.
  2) Segment + hierarchical summarization (recommended default): split long doc into overlapping chunks, generate chunk summaries then synthesize — reduces truncation and keeps latency bounded.

- Eval plan (2 weeks)
  Week 0: onboarding & secure ingest (VPC/S3). Confirming dataset format and PII redaction level.
  Week 1: Baseline runs (100 docs) across both models, collect ROUGE, entity-precision, P50/P95/P99 latency, token cost.
  Week 2: Run failure mode tests (docs at 120k/200k), evaluate stitching artifacts, tuning prompts + cache config, produce final recommendation.

- Deliverables
  * Eval report with fidelity tables, truncation incidence, and cost per summarized doc.
  * Prompt set we used (we'll include clinician-rated gold prompts).
  * Recommended production config (quantization, batching, cache TTLs).

Attachments: eval-scope.md (contains test matrix and sample prompts).

I also added two related links for internal reference: benchmark results for long-window summarization and a prior stitch-pattern doc.

Neha
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Mutual action plan (dates tentative)
- Aug 3: Redwood receives Drive sample + MedTech eval checklist (Julia).
- Aug 4: Redwood completes security onboarding (VPC link, access controls) and confirms NDA/POC terms.
- Aug 5: Quick sync (30m) to confirm prompts and SLOs; if you prefer Aug 6 that works too.
- Aug 10–17: Baseline & failure mode runs (Neha/Dylan lead).
- Aug 18: Consolidated eval report and recommendation.

Key risks / mitigation items we will surface in the baseline:
- Truncation artifacts — we'll measure incidence and show sample failure cases. Recommended mitigation: hierarchical summarization + prefix caching; will include a cost/quality tradeoff table.
- Entity loss for medications/diagnoses — we'll run entity-precision tests and tune prompts to prioritize recall for those fields.

Please confirm acceptance of the timeline and whether MedTechCo can share the sample by Aug 3 close of business. Once we have the dataset I'll send a formal HubSpot update and open the POC ticket so finance/legal can triage procurement paperwork.

Best,
Marcus Lin
